questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Irrigation and Drainage
questions.question:
Match List-I (Form of soil water) with List-II (Description).

List-I
(A) Gravitational water
(B) Capillary water
(C) Hygroscopic water
(D) Water vapour

List-II
(I) Held in small pores and available to plants
(II) Drains away quickly through large pores
(III) Present in the soil air
(IV) Held as a thin film so tightly that plants cannot use it
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)
Why: Gravitational water drains away (II). Capillary water is held in small pores and used by plants (I). Hygroscopic water is held too tightly (IV). Water vapour is in the soil air (III).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps gravitational and capillary. Option (C) swaps capillary and hygroscopic. Option (D) swaps hygroscopic and vapour.
Key point: Capillary water is the plant's main supply.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Seed Science
questions.sub_topic: Seed with more than one embryo
questions.question: Some seeds contain more than one embryo (polyembryony). This is common in:
options: B) wheat, rice and other cereals
C) pea, gram and other pulses
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) citrus and some mangoes
Why: Citrus and many south Indian mangoes produce extra embryos from nucellar tissue, giving true-to-type seedlings.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) normally have a single embryo per seed.
Key point: Nucellar embryos give uniform rootstocks.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Field Crops: Cultivation, Protection and Post-harvest
questions.question:
Match List-I (Cropping system) with List-II (Description).

List-I
(A) Intercropping
(B) Mixed cropping
(C) Relay cropping
(D) Sequential cropping

List-II
(I) Crops are grown one after another on the same land in a year
(II) The next crop is sown into the standing crop before it is harvested
(III) Two or more crops are grown together in a definite row pattern
(IV) Seeds of two or more crops are mixed and sown without rows
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: Intercropping uses a definite row pattern (III). Mixed cropping sows mixed seeds without rows (IV). Relay cropping sows the next crop before harvest (II). Sequential cropping grows crops one after another (I).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps intercropping and mixed cropping. Option (B) swaps mixed and relay cropping. Option (D) swaps relay and sequential cropping.
Key point: Rows separate intercropping from mixed cropping.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Horticulture: Importance, Orchards, Gardens and Propagation
questions.question: Spreading black polythene or dry leaves around fruit trees mainly helps to:
options: A) attract more pollinating insects to the trees
B) raise the soil pH to correct acidity
C) conserve soil moisture and suppress weeds
D) increase the size of the leaves and fruits
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) conserve soil moisture and suppress weeds
Why: Mulch reduces evaporation and blocks light to weeds.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are not its purpose.
Key point: Mulch saves water and cuts weeds.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Field Crops: Cultivation, Protection and Post-harvest
questions.sub_topic: Grain that is not a millet
questions.question: Millets are small-seeded cereals. Which of the following is NOT a millet?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Barley
Why: Barley is a temperate cereal, not a millet.
Why not the others: (B) ragi, (C) bajra and (D) kodo are millets.
Key point: Barley is a cereal like wheat.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Field Crops: Cultivation, Protection and Post-harvest
questions.question: Basmati is a famous aromatic variety group of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) rice
Why: Basmati rice is known for its long grains and aroma.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are other cereals.
Key point: Basmati — aromatic rice.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Microbiology
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Some fungi cause plant diseases such as rusts and smuts.
(B) Some bacteria decompose crop residues.
(C) Some soil microbes produce substances that promote plant growth.
(D) Viruses can be killed with antibiotics.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) are true. (D) is false: antibiotics act on bacteria, not viruses.
Why not the others: Options (B), (C) and (D) include the false statement (D).
Key point: Antibiotics do not work against viruses.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Genetics and Plant Breeding
questions.question: Bread wheat (*Triticum aestivum*) is a:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) hexaploid
Why: Bread wheat has six sets of chromosomes (2n = 6x = 42), from three ancestral species.
Why not the others: (A) has two sets; (C) three; (D) one.
Key point: Bread wheat — hexaploid.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Horticulture: Importance, Orchards, Gardens and Propagation
questions.question: Which tool is used to cut the grass of a lawn evenly?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Lawn mower
Why: A lawn mower cuts grass to an even height.
Why not the others: (A) digs; (B) weeds; (C) is for budding.
Key point: Mower — lawn care.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Biochemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (Sugar) with List-II (Common source).

List-I
(A) Fructose
(B) Maltose
(C) Lactose
(D) Sucrose

List-II
(I) Sugarcane
(II) Fruits and honey
(III) Milk
(IV) Germinating grain (malt)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(III), (D)-(I)
Why: Fructose is the fruit sugar (II). Maltose forms in germinating grain (IV). Lactose is milk sugar (III). Sucrose comes from sugarcane (I).
Why not the others: Option (B) swaps fructose and maltose. Option (C) swaps maltose and lactose. Option (D) swaps lactose and sucrose.
Key point: Fruit — fructose; malt — maltose; milk — lactose; cane — sucrose.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Scope, Importance and Breeds
questions.question: A female pig that has given birth is called a:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) sow
Why: An adult female pig is a sow; a male is a boar.
Why not the others: (A) is a female horse; (C) a female sheep; (D) a female goat or rabbit.
Key point: Sow — pig; ewe — sheep.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Cultivation of Fruits, Vegetables and Flowers
questions.question:
Match List-I (Flower) with List-II (Main use).

List-I
(A) Rose
(B) Jasmine
(C) Marigold
(D) Orchids

List-II
(I) Perfume concrete and garlands
(II) Pigment (xanthophyll) for poultry feed, and garlands
(III) Long-lasting cut flowers
(IV) Gulkand and rose water
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III)
Why: Rose gives gulkand and rose water (IV). Jasmine is used for perfume and garlands (I). Marigold gives a pigment for poultry feed (II). Orchids are long-lasting cut flowers (III).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps rose and jasmine. Option (C) swaps jasmine and marigold. Option (D) swaps marigold and orchids.
Key point: Flowers have uses beyond decoration.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Seed Science
questions.question:
Arrange the steps of seed certification in the correct order.
(A) Field inspection of the seed crop
(B) Applying to the seed certification agency
(C) Sampling and laboratory testing of the seed
(D) Tagging and sealing the seed bags
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (B), (A), (C), (D)
Why: The grower applies to the agency (B), the crop is inspected in the field (A), the cleaned seed is sampled and tested (C), and approved lots are tagged and sealed (D).
Why not the others: Option (A) inspects before applying. Option (C) tests before field inspection. Option (D) tags before testing.
Key point: Apply → inspect → test → tag.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Fruit and Vegetable Preservation
questions.question: Table and seed potatoes are commonly kept in cold stores at about:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 2–4 °C
Why: At about 2–4 °C, potatoes stay dormant and keep for months without sprouting or rotting.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) are too warm; (C) would freeze and destroy the tubers.
Key point: Potato cold storage ≈ 2–4 °C.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Genetics and Plant Breeding
questions.question: India's national gene bank for conserving crop germplasm is maintained by the:
options: A) NBPGR (plant genetic resources bureau), New Delhi
B) National Dairy Development Board, Anand
D) Central Soil Salinity Research Institute, Karnal
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) NBPGR (plant genetic resources bureau), New Delhi
Why: NBPGR conserves crop seeds and other plant genetic resources in its long-term gene bank.
Why not the others: (B) works on dairying; (C) on weather; (D) on salt-affected soils.
Key point: NBPGR — custodian of India's crop germplasm.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Agrometeorology
questions.sub_topic: Where snowfall is common in India
questions.question: In India, regular winter snowfall occurs mainly in the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Himalayan mountains
Why: Only the high Himalayas are cold enough for regular snowfall in winter.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) are far too warm for snow.
Key point: Snow — the high Himalayas.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Genetics and Plant Breeding
questions.sub_topic: Alleles and dominance — which statements are wrong
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Alleles are alternative forms of the same gene.
(B) A dominant allele is expressed even in a heterozygote.
(C) An organism's genotype can always be told from its phenotype.
(D) In codominance, only one allele is expressed in the heterozygote.
Which of the statements given above are NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (C) and (D) only
Why: (A) and (B) are true. (C) is false: a dominant phenotype may be homozygous or heterozygous. (D) is false: in codominance both alleles are expressed.
Why not the others: Options (A) and (D) call true statements wrong. Option (B) misses statement (D).
Key point: Same phenotype can hide different genotypes.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Microbiology
questions.sub_topic: Why a compost heap gets hot
questions.question: Why does the inside of a well-made compost heap become hot?
options: A) Because sunlight is trapped inside the heap
B) Because the farmer adds hot water every day
C) Because chemical fertilizers burn inside the heap
D) Because microbes breaking down the material release heat
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Because microbes breaking down the material release heat
Why: Rapid microbial decomposition releases heat, and the heap can reach 60–70 °C, which kills many weed seeds and pathogens.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are not the cause.
Key point: Hot compost = active microbes.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Care, Management and Diseases
questions.question: Biosecurity keeps diseases out of a poultry farm. Which of the following is NOT a biosecurity measure?
options: A) A disinfectant footbath at the shed entrance
B) Restricting visitors to the sheds
C) Rearing birds in all-in, all-out batches
D) Letting wild birds mix freely with the flock
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Letting wild birds mix freely with the flock
Why: Wild birds can bring in diseases such as bird flu, so contact should be prevented.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) all reduce disease entry.
Key point: Keep germs, visitors and wild birds out.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Agrometeorology
questions.question: Under which weather conditions is evaporation from a moist soil surface highest?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Hot, dry and windy
Why: Heat supplies energy, dry air takes up more vapour, and wind carries moist air away.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) each have at least one condition that slows evaporation.
Key point: Hot, dry, windy days dry out soils fastest.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Biochemistry
questions.question: Which vitamin contains the metal cobalt?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Vitamin B₁₂
Why: Vitamin B₁₂ (cobalamin) has a cobalt atom at its centre; rumen microbes need cobalt to make it.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) contain no cobalt.
Key point: Cobalt → vitamin B₁₂.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Artificial Insemination and Livestock Products
questions.question: The fat content of milk is commonly measured by the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Gerber method
Why: The Gerber test uses sulphuric acid and a centrifuge to separate fat, which is read on a butyrometer.
Why not the others: (A) MBRT judges bacterial quality; (B) Kjeldahl measures nitrogen (protein); (D) biuret detects protein.
Key point: Gerber → milk fat.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Care, Management and Diseases
questions.question: Why are cattle usually vaccinated against haemorrhagic septicaemia and black quarter before the monsoon?
options: A) Because vaccines work properly only in cold, dry weather
B) Because these diseases break out mostly in the rainy season
C) Because animals give no milk at all during the monsoon months
D) Because the vaccines are supplied free of cost only in May
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Because these diseases break out mostly in the rainy season
Why: Outbreaks of HS and BQ peak in hot, humid rainy weather, so animals are protected in advance.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are not true.
Key point: Vaccinate ahead of the risky season.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Cultivation of Fruits, Vegetables and Flowers
questions.question: The coconut palm is called ________ ('tree of heaven') because almost every part of it is useful.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) kalpavriksha
Why: Coconut gives food, oil, coir, timber and thatch, so it is called kalpavriksha.
Why not the others: (B) refers to the peepal tree; (C) is a tree-planting festival; (D) is not this title.
Key point: Coconut — kalpavriksha.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Artificial Insemination and Livestock Products
questions.question:
Arrange the steps of making ghee from butter in the correct order.
(A) Filtering out the brown residue
(B) Cooling and packing the ghee
(C) Heating the butter to drive off moisture
(D) Collecting the butter
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (D), (C), (A), (B)
Why: Butter is collected (D), heated to drive off water (C), the residue is filtered out (A), and the ghee is cooled and packed (B).
Why not the others: Option (B) heats before collecting. Option (C) filters before heating. Option (D) packs before filtering.
Key point: Butter → heat → filter → pack.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Weed Control
questions.sub_topic: Life spans of weeds — which statement is wrong
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Annual weeds complete their life cycle in one season.
(B) Biennial weeds complete their life cycle in two years.
(C) Perennial weeds live for more than two years.
(D) Weeds never act as hosts for crop pests and diseases.
Which of the statements given above is NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (D) only
Why: (D) is false: many weeds harbour insects and pathogens that attack crops. (A), (B) and (C) are true.
Why not the others: Statements (A), (B) and (C) are correct.
Key point: Weeds are classified by life span.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Care, Management and Diseases
questions.question:
Arrange the steps of making hay in the correct order.
(A) Stacking or baling the dried fodder
(B) Cutting the fodder crop at flowering
(C) Storing it under a shelter
(D) Drying it in the field with regular turning
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (B), (D), (A), (C)
Why: The crop is cut at flowering (B), dried with turning (D), stacked or baled (A), and stored under shelter (C).
Why not the others: Option (A) bales before drying. Option (B) dries before cutting. Option (D) stores before baling.
Key point: Cut → dry → bale → store.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Biochemistry
questions.sub_topic: Energy from a gram of fat
questions.question: One gram of fat gives about ________ kcal of energy, more than twice as much as a gram of carbohydrate.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 9
Why: Fats give about 9 kcal per gram; carbohydrates and proteins give about 4.
Why not the others: (A) and (D) are wrong; (B) is the value for carbohydrate or protein.
Key point: Fat ≈ 9 kcal/g; carbohydrate ≈ 4 kcal/g.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Scope, Importance and Breeds
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Broilers are reared for meat.
(B) Good commercial layers can lay about 300 eggs a year.
(C) India is among the top egg-producing countries in the world.
(D) Poultry farming needs large areas of grazing land.
Which of the statements given above is NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (D) only
Why: (D) is false: poultry is kept in compact houses and needs little land. (A), (B) and (C) are true.
Why not the others: Statements (A), (B) and (C) are correct.
Key point: Poultry suits landless and small farmers.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Microbiology
questions.sub_topic: Number of cells in a bacterium
questions.question: A bacterium is made up of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) a single cell
Why: Bacteria are single-celled (unicellular) organisms.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) are wrong; (D) describes viruses, which are not made of cells.
Key point: Bacteria are unicellular.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Soil, Soil Fertility, Fertilizers and Manures
questions.question: The soil layer that is richest in organic matter and most important for crop roots is the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) topsoil
Why: Topsoil contains most of the humus, roots and soil organisms.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) are rock; (C) subsoil has less organic matter.
Key point: Protect the topsoil.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Cultivation of Fruits, Vegetables and Flowers
questions.sub_topic: Why onions are cured before storage
questions.question: Why are onion bulbs cured (dried with their tops) for some days after harvest before storage?
options: A) Because curing increases the size and weight of the bulbs
B) Because curing makes the onions much sweeter for eating raw
C) Because dry necks and scales cut rotting and sprouting
D) Because only cured onions can be sown again as seed
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Because dry necks and scales cut rotting and sprouting
Why: Curing dries the neck and outer skins, sealing the bulb against moisture loss and storage rots.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) are not effects; (D) bulbs are not seed.
Key point: Cure onions before storing them.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Soil, Soil Fertility, Fertilizers and Manures
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) A fertile soil may be unproductive if it is waterlogged.
(B) Soil fertility is the soil's ability to supply nutrients to plants.
(C) Productivity depends on fertility as well as management and climate.
(D) Every fertile soil is also productive.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) are true. (D) is false: a fertile soil can still give poor yields because of waterlogging, salinity, poor management or bad weather.
Why not the others: Options (A), (B) and (D) include the false statement (D).
Key point: Fertility is needed for productivity but does not guarantee it.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Genetics and Plant Breeding
questions.question: Offspring resemble their parents because of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) heredity
Why: Heredity passes traits from parents to offspring through genes.
Why not the others: (A) creates changes; (B) and (D) are unrelated processes.
Key point: Heredity = passing on of traits.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Agrometeorology
questions.question:
Match List-I (IMD warning colour) with List-II (Meaning).

List-I
(A) Green
(B) Yellow
(C) Orange
(D) Red

List-II
(I) Be updated about the weather
(II) Take action
(III) No warning; no action needed
(IV) Be prepared
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)
Why: Green means no warning (III). Yellow means be updated (I). Orange means be prepared (IV). Red means take action (II).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps green and yellow. Option (C) swaps yellow and orange. Option (D) swaps orange and red.
Key point: Warnings rise from green to red.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Irrigation and Drainage
questions.sub_topic: Overall efficiency of an irrigation system
questions.question: In an irrigation system, the conveyance efficiency is 80% and the field application efficiency is 75%. What is the overall irrigation efficiency?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 60%
Why: Step 1: overall efficiency = conveyance × application.
Step 2: 0.80 × 0.75 = 0.60, i.e. 60%.
Why not the others: (A) adds the two; (B) averages them; (D) subtracts them.
Key point: Losses multiply along the system.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Fruit and Vegetable Preservation
questions.question:
Arrange the steps of making mango pickle in the correct order.
(A) Filling into clean, dry jars
(B) Keeping the jars in the sun for some days to mature
(C) Washing and cutting the mangoes
(D) Mixing with salt, spices and oil
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (C), (D), (A), (B)
Why: Mangoes are washed and cut (C), mixed with salt, spices and oil (D), filled into jars (A), and matured in the sun (B).
Why not the others: Option (A) fills jars before mixing. Option (B) mixes before cutting. Option (C) suns before filling.
Key point: Cut → mix → fill → mature.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Horticulture: Importance, Orchards, Gardens and Propagation
questions.sub_topic: Training systems for fruit trees — which hold
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) The open-centre system lets light into the middle of the canopy.
(B) In the central-leader system, a main trunk grows up through the tree with branches around it.
(C) The modified-leader system combines features of the other two.
(D) Training is done only on old, bearing trees.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) are true. (D) is false: training is done on young trees to shape their framework.
Why not the others: Options (B), (C) and (D) include the false statement (D).
Key point: Choose the training system to suit the fruit and the site.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Soil, Soil Fertility, Fertilizers and Manures
questions.sub_topic: Tool for nitrogen management in rice
questions.question: The leaf colour chart (LCC) helps rice farmers decide:
options: A) when to apply nitrogen fertilizer
B) the right time to harvest the crop
C) which rice variety to sow next season
D) how deep the field should be ploughed
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) when to apply nitrogen fertilizer
Why: Farmers match leaf greenness with the chart's shades and top-dress nitrogen when leaves are paler than the threshold.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) are not decided by the LCC.
Key point: LCC = need-based nitrogen.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Scope, Importance and Breeds
questions.question: Mohair fibre is obtained from the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Angora goat
Why: The Angora goat produces long, lustrous mohair.
Why not the others: (A) gives fine wool; (B) gives pashmina; (C) gives coarse hair and down.
Key point: Angora goat — mohair.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Fisheries
questions.question: Pearls are cultured in:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) oysters and mussels
Why: A nucleus is placed in a pearl oyster or freshwater mussel, which coats it with nacre to form a pearl.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) do not make pearls.
Key point: Pearl culture uses molluscs.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Weed Control
questions.question: For spraying herbicides evenly over the soil or weeds, the recommended nozzle on a knapsack sprayer is the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) flat-fan nozzle
Why: A flat-fan nozzle gives an even band of spray, suited to herbicides; hollow-cone nozzles suit insecticides and fungicides.
Why not the others: (A) gives fine droplets that drift; (C) gives a jet; (D) is for irrigation.
Key point: Flat-fan for herbicides.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Irrigation and Drainage
questions.question: The Central Soil Salinity Research Institute (CSSRI), which works on reclaiming salt-affected soils, is located at:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Karnal
Why: CSSRI is at Karnal in Haryana.
Why not the others: (B) hosts the rice research institute; (C) the arid zone institute; (D) the potato research institute.
Key point: CSSRI — Karnal.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Care, Management and Diseases
questions.question:
Match List-I (Parasite) with List-II (Description).

List-I
(A) Tick
(B) Liver fluke
(C) Roundworm
(D) Lice

List-II
(I) Internal worm living in the intestine
(II) Tiny wingless insects living among the hair
(III) Internal flatworm that damages the liver
(IV) External parasite that sucks blood and spreads diseases
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Why: Ticks suck blood and spread diseases (IV). Liver flukes damage the liver (III). Roundworms live in the intestine (I). Lice live among the hair (II).
Why not the others: Option (B) swaps tick and liver fluke. Option (C) swaps liver fluke and roundworm. Option (D) swaps roundworm and lice.
Key point: Control both external and internal parasites.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Genetics and Plant Breeding
questions.sub_topic: Item that is not part of a chromosome
questions.question: A chromosome has several parts. Which of the following is NOT a part of a chromosome?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Chloroplast
Why: A chloroplast is a separate organelle for photosynthesis.
Why not the others: (A) joins the chromatids; (B) is one of the two copies; (C) caps the ends.
Key point: Centromere, chromatids and telomeres belong to chromosomes.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Crop Production: Introduction and Modern Agriculture
questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

Conservation agriculture and precision agriculture both aim to grow more with fewer resources. Conservation agriculture disturbs the soil as little as possible, keeps it covered with crop residues and diversifies the crops grown. In north-west India, burning rice straw after harvest has been common because it clears the field quickly for wheat, but the smoke pollutes the air over a large region, and the soil loses organic matter and useful organisms. Keeping the residue on the surface instead protects the soil from erosion, conserves moisture and slowly adds organic matter. Precision agriculture treats each part of a field according to its needs. Laser land levellers give a smooth, uniformly sloped field so that water spreads evenly; levelled fields need about 25 percent less irrigation water and give more even crop stands. Grid soil sampling and satellite or drone images are used to prepare maps showing zones of low and high fertility. Variable-rate applicators then put more fertilizer only where the map shows it is needed, and less elsewhere. Drones are also used to spray pesticides and nutrients over small areas quickly, and soil-moisture sensors can tell farmers when to irrigate. These technologies cost money, so custom-hiring centres and farmer groups help small farmers use them.

Question: According to the passage, what is a benefit of laser land levelling?
options: A) Water spreads evenly and about 25% less water is needed
B) It removes all of the weeds from the field without any herbicides
C) It doubles the nitrogen content of the soil within one season
D) It allows the rice straw to be burnt much more quickly after harvest
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Water spreads evenly and about 25% less water is needed
Why: The passage says levelled fields let water spread evenly and need about 25 percent less irrigation water.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) are not stated.
Key point: A level field means even water and an even crop.

questions.sub_topic: Why keep residue instead of burning

Question: Why does the passage favour keeping rice residue on the field rather than burning it?
options: A) Because residue left lying on the field kills all of the insect pests
B) Because burning the straw makes the next wheat crop ripen far too early
C) Because residue protects soil and moisture, while burning pollutes the air
D) Because the government pays farmers for every tonne of straw left behind
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Because residue protects soil and moisture, while burning pollutes the air
Why: The passage says burning pollutes the air and robs the soil of organic matter, while residue on the surface protects the soil, conserves moisture and adds organic matter.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are not stated.
Key point: Residue is a resource, not waste.

Question: According to the passage, drones are used in precision agriculture to:
options: A) plough the field and sow the seed in rows
B) spray crops and take images for field maps
C) harvest the crop and thresh out the grain
D) carry the farm produce to distant markets
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) spray crops and take images for field maps
Why: The passage says drone images help make fertility maps and drones spray pesticides and nutrients over small areas.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are not mentioned.
Key point: Drones see and spray.

Question: A 2-hectare field normally needs 50 cm of irrigation water in a season. Using the saving given in the passage, how much water is saved after laser levelling? (1 hectare-centimetre = 100 m³)
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 2,500 m³
Why: Step 1: depth saved = 50 × 25 ÷ 100 = 12.5 cm.
Step 2: volume saved = 12.5 ha-cm per ha × 2 ha = 25 ha-cm.
Step 3: 25 × 100 = 2,500 m³.
Why not the others: (A) is ten times too small; (B) is the total water for the field; (C) is the saving for one hectare only.
Key point: Saving = depth × share saved × area.

These technologies cost money, so custom-hiring centres and farmer groups help small farmers use them.

Question: A fertility map of a field shows that the northern half is low in nitrogen and the southern half is high. Which action follows the variable-rate approach described in the passage?
options: A) Apply exactly the same dose of nitrogen to the whole field
B) Apply nitrogen only to the southern half, which is already high
C) Apply more nitrogen to the north and less to the south
D) Stop applying any nitrogen fertilizer to the field altogether
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Apply more nitrogen to the north and less to the south
Why: The passage says variable-rate applicators put more fertilizer where the map shows it is needed and less elsewhere.
Why not the others: (A) ignores the map; (B) reverses it; (D) would starve the low-nitrogen half.
Key point: Precision farming = right dose in the right place.
